messages:
maya: heads-up — got a bunch of alerts 10m ago where the tool-invocation path returned a malformed structured response and our router immediately failed over to the fallback model, doubling cost for those requests. Seeing it on friday-peak.
lin: ugh — any sample payloads? can we repro locally?
maya: logged one example in the infra logs. short version: tool returned JSON with an extra trailing comma and our parser throws, we mark as "schema_reject" and immediate fallback kicks in. log snippet:
```
REQUEST id=abc123 model=rl-serve-1 route=toolflow
RESP tool=search-tool status=200 body="{\"top_hit\": \"file.txt\",}"
PARSE ERROR: Trailing comma at position 24
FALLBACK: routing to baseline-gpt-small
COST: +2x tokens
```
maya: curious thing — router telemetry shows those requests still counted against the original route's quota even though fallback served them. that screws quota-slas and "route-level" chargebacks.
samir: exactly — we have two problems: (1) strict parser error handling is brittle for minor malformations; (2) billing/quotas are tied to initial routing decision rather than final serving. both feel wrong.
jonah: do we have a spec for how to attribute cost when fallback happens? i thought fallback should attribute to the final model that generated tokens.
alexa: current invoicing design: charge where request was accepted (route owner). This made chargebacks straightforward but assumes no fallback. we can change but it's a product + infra lift.
lin: quick mitigation: can we do a forgiving parse for tool responses (try a quick JSON sanitize) and only fallback when truly incompatible? that would avoid most of these tiny errors.
maya: sandboxed sanitize would help. but also need to surface the original tool response in console for debugging — right now console's structured-output dashboard only shows "schema_reject" counts, not the raw payloads.
samir: +1 on raw payloads but we need to be careful with PII. should redact keys like email, ssn. maybe store sanitized payloads in limited retention for 7d.
jonah: telemetry side: we saw spikes in "schema_reject" metric at 15:03 for route customer-search-prod. alert noise because threshold is low. we should offer a per-route sampling/aggregation to avoid paging on known bad clients.
alexa: for rollouts UX: when we flip strict schema enforcement on by default, ops will need a canary that logs but doesn't fallback. maybe three states: permissive (log only), strict (reject+fallback), strict-attribute (reject+no-fallback) — need names.
lin: can we implement "log-only" at routing layer by default for new routes and add a console toggle? then product can graduate routes to strict.
maya: agree. small plan proposal:
  - short term: implement harmless JSON sanitizer + try-parse path (router-level). 48h
  - mid term: attribution change: bill final serving model when fallback happens; requires infra conf change and billing sync, ETA 2 sprints
  - UX: add console toggle with three states (permissive/log-only, strict+fallback, strict+no-fallback). include safe redaction of raw payloads in logs. ETA 1 sprint for initial UI.
samir: +1. also we should emit a new telemetry dimension: "final_model" in the schema_reject event so we can query how many rejected requests actually fell back.
jonah: implementation note: if we sanitize and reformat JSON, we must still include original checksum/hash so we can trace back to original raw log for incident reviews.
alexa: product/finance — changing attribution affects billing.csv; need a migration plan to avoid double-billing windows. We'll need to surface changes in the console Billing FAQ.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/sanitize-toolresponses (canary) -> infra-canary (ETA 2h)
lin: sweet. i'll pair with infra on the canary. maya i'll take the console toggle prototype.
maya: thanks. filing followups:
  - GH issue: infra/sanitize-toolresponses (includes tests for trailing commas, single quotes, unescaped newlines)
  - GH issue: billing/attribute-finalmodel
  - ENG-PLAT: add telemetry "final_model" and sample retention policy
jonah: also add an automated smoke test that simulates malformed tool output so we don't regress.
maya: ok will drop those issues. good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
